newsitem.title: JAPAN: SOCCER-THREE TEAMS STAY UNBEATEN IN J.LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-THREE TEAMS STAY UNBEATEN IN J.LEAGUE.

text.p: Brazilian midfielder Valber scored two late goals to help Yokohama Flugels defeat Vissel Kobe 3-1 and stay unbeaten after three rounds of first-stage competition in Japan's J.League on Saturday.
Gamba Osaka, led by Cameroon forward Patrick Mboma, and 1996 champions Kashima Antlers also extended their unbeaten records.
Gamba pulled off their third successive four-goal game in defeating Shimizu S-Pulse 4-1 to remain top of the table, leading the other unbeaten squads on goal difference.

Kashima beat Nagoya Grampus Eight 2-0 away with goals coming from Brazilian Mazinho. Nagoya, last year's runner-up and one of the title favorites this season, have lost all three of their matches in the new season.
Yokohama Marinos came back from a two-goal deficit to beat Verdy Kawasaki on penalties, winning the shoot-out 4-2.
Cerezo Osaka downed Iwata 2-1, winning a come-from-behind victory with two goals from Akinori Nishizawa.
Takuya Takagi scored his first goal of the season three minutes from time as Hiroshima downed Urawa 1-0.
Hiratsuka won 2-0 over Purple Sanga, thanks to a strike by Brazilian Lopes and an own goal.
Brazilian defender Jamelli's 70th-minute header gave Kashiwa a 2-1 win over Fukuoka.
